title: Token cadence benchmarking suite with p95/p99 regression guardrails
creator: Liam Zhang
description: Build a reproducible tokens-per-second benchmarking suite that captures token cadence across representative sequence-length distributions and microburst patterns, stores deterministic snapshots (golden traces), and raises regressions on p95/p99 token generation latency and sustained TPS. This ticket implements the benchmark runner, snapshot storage, CI gating, and an automated regression detector tied into Slack/PagerDuty. Non-goals: full end-to-end production load testing (handled by separate load-test infra), per-model training optimizations, or replacing existing smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark runner can execute canonical scenarios for at least 6 core models and emit per-token timestamps and CPU/GPU utilization metrics.
Snapshots (golden traces) are stored in an immutable bucket with metadata (model, seq profile, seed, hw profile) and have a UUID reference.
Automated regression detector evaluates new runs vs golden traces and opens an alert when p95 latency regresses >8% or sustained TPS drops >10% for a model/variant.
CI gate integration: any PR touching runtime or model packaging that changes measured TPS/p95 by >10% must be blocked and create a review task with a perf-run attached.
Dashboards in Grafana show historical p50/p95/p99 and TPS with annotation points for goldens and flagged regressions.
Runbook/Playbook created with step-by-step triage for performance alerts and rollbacks (link provided).
tasks: Design canonical workloads and sequence-length mix (short/medium/long/microburst). Reference: confluence/runtime/perf/token-cadence-design.
Implement runner agent that emits per-token timing + KV cache hit/miss annotations; add deterministic seeding for non-random sampling.
Create snapshot storage schema and immutability policy in S3 GCS bucket; include small metadata index in Postgres.
Build regression detector service (statistical comparator + threshold rules) and wire to alerting channel.
Add CI job 'tps-cadence-smoke' that runs lightweight scenarios on PRs and reports diffs to GitHub checks.
Create Grafana dashboards and set up alert rules; link to playbook and PagerDuty integration.
Run full sweep across 6 core models, capture baseline, and publish results to Confluence and internal benchmark catalog.
comments: 2026-03-03 — Liam Zhang: Kickoff meeting done. Agreed on three sequence profiles (16, 128, 1024) plus a synthetic microburst pattern. Owner: Asha for runner, Marco for CI integration.

2026-03-05 — Asha Patel: Initial prototype runner emits per-token timestamps and the KV-cache annotation. See draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Needs perf overhead measurement.

2026-03-07 — Marco Alvarez: CI job drafted in .github/workflows/tps-cadence.yml, using a small n1-standard instance. CI durations ~6m for a single model short profile. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/310.

2026-03-08 — Design feedback (Priya Singh): Add golden versioning scheme v{major}.{minor}-{commit-short} and include allocator/hw-labels in metadata. Also ensure snapshots are <50MB compressed for quick retrieval.

2026-03-09 — Asha Patel: Spike measured runner overhead ~3% p50 but 6% p95 for long sequences on a40. Plan: sample every Nth token for long runs to reduce instrumentation overhead, store full traces for short/microburst workloads.

2026-03-10 — Liam Zhang: Decided on regression thresholds: p95 >8% or p99 >12% (or sustained TPS drop >10%) to reduce noise. Will use bootstrap for statistical confidence and require at least 3 repeated runs to trigger an alert.

2026-03-11 — QA (Maya Chen): Ran sanity pass against models: 'redwood-lite-v1', 'rw-open-7b', 'rw-open-13b', 'rw-compat-ocr'. Results uploaded: https://confluence.redwood/workbench/token-cadence/baselines. A few models had high variance; scheduling re-runs overnight.
2026-03-12 — Security (Ravi Kumar): Reviewed snapshot storage plan. No secrets stored; IAM policy minimal read/write for perf-bot. Recommend periodic audit; security_review_required=false.
2026-03-12 — Asha Patel: Next steps: finalize PRs, land CI job as optional for next week, and schedule a perf-review with Runtime team on 2026-03-18.
